simple.meaning: שָׁסַע (shâçaʻ) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to split or tear ; figuratively, to upbraid.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 9 times across Leviticus, Deuteronomy, Judges, 1 Samuel, beginning at Leviticus 1:17. Its contexts include offering, altar, priesthood.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to שָׁסַע (H8156).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: שָׁסַע (shâçaʻ) / H8156 is traced through Leviticus 1:17, Leviticus 11:3, Leviticus 11:7, Leviticus 11:26 as a generated source-based concept entry.

timeline.evidenceText: He shall tear it by its wings, but shall not divide it apart. The priest shall burn it on the altar, on the wood that is on the fire. It is a burnt offering, an offering made by fire, of a pleasant aroma to Yahweh.
Whatever parts the hoof, and is cloven-footed, and chews the cud among the animals, that you may eat.
The pig, because it has a split hoof, and is cloven-footed, but doesn’t chew the cud, is unclean to you.
“ ‘Every animal which has a split hoof that isn’t completely divided, or doesn’t chew the cud, is unclean to you. Everyone who touches them shall be unclean.
Every animal that parts the hoof, and has the hoof split in two and chews the cud, among the animals, you may eat.

Nevertheless these you shall not eat of them that chew the cud, or of those who have the hoof split: the camel, the hare, and the rabbit. Because they chew the cud but don’t part the hoof, they are unclean to you.
Yahweh’s Spirit came mightily on him, and he tore him as he would have torn a young goat with his bare hands, but he didn’t tell his father or his mother what he had done.

definitions.short: to split or tear ; figuratively, to upbraid
definitions.full: H8156. shasa [ שָׁסַע ] verb divide, cleave (Late Hebrew Pi`el tear spart ; ᵑ7 Jer Pa`el Lam 3:11 tear in pieces (for HCT מִּשֵּׁחַ )); — Qal Participle (with accusative of congnate meaning with verb שֶׁ֫סַע ): masculine singular מַּרְסָה שֶׁסַע וְשֹׁסַע Lev 11:7 (P; on ׳שֹׁ compare Lag BN 84 ) cleaving the cleft of the hoof , i.e. having cloven hoof, so feminine singular שֹׁסַ֫עַת 11:3 , compare Deut 14:6 ; שֹׁסַ֫עַת אֵינֶנָּה שֶׁסַע Lev 11:26 (P); passive הַשְּׁסוּעָה הַמַּרְסָה Deut 14:7 . Pi`el tear in two , a lion, kid, Imperfect, Infinitive construct הַגְּדִי כְּשַׁסַּע וַיְשַׁסְּעֵהוּ Judg 14:6 ; a bird (by, or at, its wings), Perfect 3masculine singular consecutive אֹתוֺ וְשִׁסַּע Lev 1:17 (P); imperfect 3masculine singular ( בַּדְּבָרִים אֶתאֲֿנָשָׁיו ) וַיְשַׁסַּע 1Sam 24:8 gives too violent a meaning; probably corrupt for word = restrain , or the like Dr HPS, compare Bu Now (hesitantly). שֶׁ֫סַע noun [masculine] cleft ; — as accusative of congnate meaning with verb with [ שָׁסַע ], q. v.; absolute Lev 11:26 , construct 11:3 ; 11:7 ; Deut 14:6 .
